L5@P0: A rotation in a binary tree is a simple and local restructuring technique
L6@P0: commonly used in computer science. We propose in this paper three restrictions on the general rotation operation. We study the case when only leftmost
L7@P0: rotations are permitted, which corresponds to a natural flipping on polygon
L8@P0: triangulations. The resulting combinatorial structure is a tree structure with
L9@P0: the root as the greatest element. We exhibit an efficient algorithm for computing the join of two trees and the minimum number of leftmost rotations
L10@P0: necessary to transform one tree into the other.

L13@P0: Rotation is one of the most common operations for restructuring binary trees. It
L14@P0: has the advantage of altering the depths of some of the nodes in the tree while
L15@P0: preserving the symmetric order of all the nodes. Thus rotation is commonly used
L16@P0: in a variety of algorithms for maintaining binary search trees with a good amortized
L17@P0: behavior [10, 24, 28].
L18@P0: The combinatorial properties of binary trees under the rotation operation have

L1@P0: LATTICES
L2@P0: EMILY BARNARD, COLIN DEFANT, AND ERIC J. HANSON
L3@P0: Abstract. The pop-stack operator of a finite lattice L is the map pop↓
L4@P0: L : L → L that sends each
L5@P0: element x ∈ L to the meet of {x} ∪ covL(x), where covL(x) is the set of elements covered by x in
L6@P0: L. We study several properties of the pop-stack operator of tors Λ, the lattice of torsion classes of
L7@P0: a τ -tilting finite algebra Λ over a field K. We describe the pop-stack operator in terms of certain
L8@P0: mutations of 2-term simple-minded collections. This allows us to describe preimages of a given
L9@P0: torsion class under the pop-stack operator.
L10@P0: We then specialize our attention to Cambrian lattices of a finite irreducible Coxeter group W.
L11@P0: Using tools from representation theory, we provide simple Coxeter-theoretic and lattice-theoretic
L12@P0: descriptions of the image of the pop-stack operator of a Cambrian lattice (which can be stated
L13@P0: without representation theory). When specialized to a bipartite Cambrian lattice of type A, this
L14@P0: result settles a conjecture of Choi and Sun. We also settle a related enumerative conjecture of
L15@P0: Defant and Williams. When L is an arbitrary lattice quotient of the weak order on W, we prove
L16@P0: that the maximum size of a forward orbit under the pop-stack operator of L is at most the Coxeter
L17@P0: number of W; when L is a Cambrian lattice, we provide an explicit construction to show that this
L18@P0: maximum forward orbit size is actually equal to the Coxeter number.
